reviews.title: No widget, no can do
reviews.text: I so wish this app had a widget option. If you are making an app for people with ADHD, a widget is not a "nice to have"—it is a life support system for many of us. “Out of sight, out of mind” is not just a saying for us; it is a neurological reality (it’s an object permanence thing). Unless my to-do list is in a widget on my Home Screen, it simply ceases to exist. As will your app. I will forget I downloaded it. I will forget I paid for it. I will forget I even have a phone. Please, give us widgets. Save us from ourselves.

With the high risk of financial fraud & abuse, I’m not willing to risk that without having the opportunity to see if the app would work for me.

reviews.title: It’s nice to feel seen - or it would have been
reviews.text: A lot of people with chronic pain or autoimmune disorders have cognitive impairments related to their diagnosis. Come to think of it, I’ve heard the same about cancer survivors for years (or forever) after chemotherapy. I’m seeking help with a form of that known as “fibro fog”. I just set up my first task, cleaning the living room - that’s the project that has been top of my list for the last three months. I told the AI to double the time estimates and it did - that’s great! …But I’m still a long ways away from having a list that looks realistic or doable. If that sounds like an impossible situation, well, it is, but I think that it’s within reach for the intake questionnaire to accommodate people in my situation. Ask some version of “preferred Pomodoro intervals” (for me, that’s 45 minutes of rest for every 15 minutes of work) and “number of Pomodoros per day” (for me, 2). That means that, for me, cleaning the living room is actually four tasks spread out over two days - tidy, dust (dry), clean (wet), and vacuum/sweep. If I could do that much, I’d still be in an impossible situation, but I would also be way better off than I am right now.

reviews.title: Needs Work
reviews.text:
The idea behind this app is good but it needs some work. For example, you cannot sync across devices, so your lists are device specific. Additionally, it asks you to pay each time you download it (although Apple only counts 1 subscription, so just look for the cheapest offer because they vary).

Overall, it has potential but it just needs to work out the kinks before it can be a good app. I would consider maybe looking at other popular productivity apps (e.g. Structured) and seeing what they do.

Idk. I don’t like giving bad reviews, but it’s a bad app. I’m so blessed that I didn’t buy one of those exceptionally expensive subscriptions, without trying it first. I don’t comprehend how there are so many great reviews. Surely you can do better. I’m sorry, I wish I could give a better review. reviews.title: Worth trying for a year

All are the same, so far it seems similar except this one has a timer and a voice reminder. I just downloaded it and it hasn’t been a day, but compared to all the other apps is the price. I’m willing to pay $20 for a year to give it a chance most are over $50 for a year. For me the price is worth giving it a chance. So thanks!!!

reviews.title: Love the AI subtasks!
reviews.text:
I have just started using the yearly subscription after using the free version. 
I am thrilled with it. The breaking down of each tasks by AI is beneficial to me. I would be able to do that on my own but it would just be another task to do before I would be able to complete my tasks list. This AI does it for me! And it makes suggestion that I would not have remembered to think about. So for me, with my anxiety paralysis, this was a big deal. Love it! Thank you, developer!!

reviews.title: Barebones but super helpful
reviews.text: I have adhd and autism and breaking down tasks is a struggle for me and a barrier to starting them. I have tried goblin tools but it just doesn’t do as good as this app does at really breaking stuff down without being redundant. Even though it’s still a super simple app with not a lot of features, I got the pro version to try out for a month to see how it goes. I just started using it but it’s super helpful so far! I love that it lets you do a task timer and I am hoping that will not only show me how long the tasks actually take me, but allow for the AI to adjust as well!

reviews.title: Great! One suggestion

I like this app a lot so far. I have moderate ADHD and really struggle with time management, so an app that focuses on timing is very helpful. I’m also using the free version and haven’t run into any paywalls yet, so that’s nice.
My one suggestion would be to be able to add tasks WITHOUT subtasks- I know subtasks are kind of the point of the app, but for me, something simple like “unload dishwasher” doesn’t need them.

reviews.title: Great app 10/10. Needs sharing across devices.
reviews.text: This app is very helpful with those with ADHD or those struggling with executive functioning. The AI tool that helps chunk and break down the main task is very helpful and accurate. The breakdown or how chunked the subtask are is based on the difficulty of the task you input. The easier or harder the task will correlate.This is  good for those with ADHD as it breaks it into smaller written task preventing overwhelm by one daunting task.  Only issue is hopefully in a future update there is cross saving and synchronization across devices. I haven’t fully explored but using the free version hasn’t interfered with using the app. If you have ADHD or struggle with procrastination or feeling overwhelmed please try this app.

reviews.title: Has potential
reviews.text: I'll start with the positive.  It's a good idea.  The AI creates subtasks so I don't have to, which can make things easier on my already overtaxed brain.  It is helpful to see how much extra time it's taken me to compete a certain step.  I'll admit though.  I bought this app, but don't use it. My number one complaint is that when the time is up for certain step of a task it sends a notification to my phone.  That's it.  I have an iPhone so all I get is a little ding.  I don't hear it or notice it, because I'm involved in an activity. I have ADHD, I forget the app is even running.  I need an alarm to go off, preferably one I can set to go off multiple times until I finish the step.  Another feature I'd like is the ability to have multiple tasks going at once.  I can only have one going at a time.  This is not ideal.  I gave it three stars because I hope it gets better.  Just a few small improvements would truly make this great.

reviews.title: Not for ADHD

reviews.title: My mental wheelchair
reviews.text:
this app is so helpful to me.  I had TBI and permanent brain damage in frontal lobe making my executive function and ADHD unmanageable.

Before my injury I was a “DataSmith” but after lost all hope, interest, motivation to claw my back.
Neurolist is my mental “wheelchair “ and given me hope.

Thank you for making my life more manageable.  The folks around me thank you too because it’s usefulness has alleviated other collateral damage from my accident, especially depression.

God bless, keep it up!

Rocket Queen 
A Neurolist ambassador

reviews.title: Intelligent AI tool
reviews.text: I have ADHD and I downloaded this months ago as it seemed like a good tool to use to manage myself. I of course didn’t use it at first because of course (ADHD). But I asked for constant reminders to use it and have always gotten them. I finally put my foot down to clean my room and created a task for it and it created subtasks to make things easier. You can change the length of them, the difficulty of the task itself, and set a reminder. The AI subtask creator can do a multitude of tasks as well like a PC Build, Feeding your Animal, and more. Any task you create it will generate subtasks for it. Thank you for constantly reminding me to use it, and I finally have.

reviews.title: Seems good-needs a prioritization feature
reviews.text: I like it so far, but a big thing I struggle with my ADHD is task prioritization. The app needs a  way for us to color-code/sort tasks by high priority, medium priority, low priority so everything isn’t lumped together in the same way. otherwise i find it be confusing/overwhelming and can’t figure out where to start. The AI could also “suggest” prioritizing if we’re unsure, maybe putting work tasks or chores like grocery and cleaning first.

This app puts in the pieces together for me. Thank you.
